title: Stovetop Leche Flan
blurb: Silky steamed egg custard under a thin layer of amber caramel.

steps.text: Lightly whisk eggs, evaporated milk, condensed milk, and vanilla. Strain into a jug. Set out a small heatproof metal mold and prepare a covered steamer.
Cook sugar and the measured water in a small light saucepan, without stirring, until medium amber. Use dry mitts and carefully pour hot caramel into the mold. Leave it untouched until hard.

Pour the egg mixture over the hardened caramel and cover the mold with foil. Steam over gently simmering water for about 25 minutes. The edges should be set and the center reach 71°C. Keep water below the mold and add hot water if needed.
Cool for 20 minutes and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Loosen the rim and invert onto a rimmed plate.

Heat the oil in a skillet and sauté the corn until steaming and slightly blistered. Stir in the scallion for the final minute.
Take off the heat, then add vinegar, chili, and a pinch of salt. Spoon into a small cup.

Heat a skillet on low. Toast the cut faces until lightly golden and fragrant, lifting the buns now and then to check.
Dust the toasted faces with cinnamon and serve warm.

title: Quick-Pickled Labanos and Carrot

steps.text: Wash and peel the radish and carrot. Slice both into thin matchsticks.
Stir cane vinegar, sugar, and salt in a container until the sugar dissolves. Toss with the vegetables and cover.
Chill for 20 minutes, then scoop into a cup to serve.

title: Nori Popcorn
blurb: Fresh popcorn tossed with crumbled seaweed and a pinch of salt.

steps.text: Crumble a plain toasted nori sheet between your palms. Measure the kernels and oil.

Warm the oil in a heavy lidded pot over medium heat. Add the kernels in an even layer, cover, and shake the pot by its handle every few seconds. Remove from the heat once there are about 2 seconds between pops.
Open the lid away from your face. Toss the hot popcorn with the nori and salt.

steps.text: Set out four pairs of crackers and break the chocolate into small pieces.
In a microwave-safe bowl, warm the chocolate in 15-second bursts, stirring after each one until smooth.
Spread a little chocolate on four crackers and sandwich with the rest.
Let the chocolate cool on the counter before serving.

title: Laswa with Squash and Okra

steps.text: Peel and cube the squash. Trim the okra, rinse the malunggay leaves, and chop tomato and onion.
Bring water, tomato, onion, and salt to a boil. Add the squash and simmer for about 6 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the okra and simmer until fork-tender. Stir in the malunggay for the final minute. Serve while the leaves are bright green.

title: Suam na Mais
blurb: Fresh corn and malunggay in a brothy Pampanga-style soup.

steps.text: Slice kernels off the corn and roughly chop half. Mince garlic and ginger, and rinse the malunggay.
Sauté the garlic and ginger in oil until fragrant, then stir in the corn and fish sauce.
Add stock, bring to a boil, and simmer for approximately 12 minutes until the corn is soft and the broth lightly thickened. Stir in malunggay in the final minute.

title: Pinangat na Bangus
blurb: Boneless bangus gently simmered in a bright tomato and calamansi broth.

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and thinly slice the ginger. Squeeze the calamansi. Cut the fish into two portions on a separate board and check for stray bones.
Layer tomato and ginger in a skillet with the measured water and salt. Bring to a simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Lay the fish on top, add most of the calamansi juice, cover, and simmer gently. Check the thickest part reaches 63°C and flakes easily. Use a little more water if the pan starts drying out.
Finish with the remaining juice and serve with freshly cooked rice. If using chilled leftover rice, reheat it separately to 74°C.

title: Chicken Pastil Bowl
blurb: A Maguindanao-inspired rice bowl topped with browned chicken kagikit.

steps.text: Finely shred the cooked chicken. Chop onion, garlic, and ginger, and set out freshly cooked rice.
Warm the oil on medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger until softened.
Add chicken, soy sauce, and pepper. Cook while tossing until the edges brown and the chicken reaches 74°C throughout.
Spoon the chicken over rice. If using chilled leftover rice, reheat it separately to 74°C.

title: Tofu Lumpiang Sariwa
blurb: Soft fresh lumpia with garlicky tofu, vegetables, and a quick peanut sauce.

steps.text: Pat tofu dry and cut into strips. Shred cabbage and carrot, rinse lettuce, and mince garlic. Set out ready-to-eat fresh lumpia wrappers.
Sauté garlic and tofu in oil until the tofu gets a little color. Add cabbage and carrot and cook until tender-crisp.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, and water into a pourable sauce. Place lettuce and filling on each wrapper, fold the bottom up, and roll. Drizzle or dip in the sauce.

title: Kinamatisang Itlog
blurb: Hard-boiled eggs simmered briefly in a chunky tomato sauce.

steps.text: Chop tomato, onion, and garlic. Set out freshly cooked rice or heat promptly chilled leftover rice to 74°C.
Cover eggs with cold water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle boil for about 10 minutes, until the yolks and whites are firm.
Cool the eggs briefly under cold running water. Peel and halve them.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, then add tomato, fish sauce, and the 40 ml water. Simmer until the tomato breaks down into a chunky sauce. Add eggs cut-side up and warm through. Spoon onto the rice.

Divide the filling between two soft tortillas. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.

title: Ginataang Puso ng Saging
blurb: Tender banana blossom simmered with ginger and coconut milk.

steps.text: Remove tough dark outer bracts and discard the stem. Slice the tender inner blossom finely, toss with the salt, and squeeze. Rinse and drain. Chop onion, garlic, ginger, and chili.
Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in oil on medium heat until fragrant.
Add the banana blossom, coconut milk, water, and chili. Simmer gently until the strips are fully tender and the sauce has reduced. Stir in cane vinegar and simmer another minute.

title: Savory Corn Grits with Cheese
blurb: Warm yellow corn grits with melted cheddar and fresh scallion.

steps.text: Grate the cheese and slice the scallion. Bring lightly salted water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Whisk in the fine corn grits and reduce to a gentle simmer. Stir regularly until the grits are smooth and tender. Follow the package if the grind needs longer.
Turn off the heat, stir in cheddar until melted, and finish with sliced scallion.

title: Kamote Peanut Breakfast Bowl
blurb: Soft sweet potato mashed with banana, milk, and peanut butter.

steps.text: Wash and scrub the sweet potato. Pierce it several times with a fork and put it on a microwave-safe plate.
Microwave on high, turning halfway through. Begin checking after 5 minutes. Continue in 1-minute bursts until a fork slides easily to the center.
Rest until cool enough to handle and carefully split open.
Scoop the flesh into a bowl, mash with milk, and top with sliced banana, peanut butter, and cinnamon.

steps.text: Flake chilled, ready-to-eat smoked bangus and remove any stray bones. Mix with yogurt, calamansi, and black pepper.
Slice the cucumber thinly. Split the rolls and fill with fish spread and cucumber.

title: Ginataang Tutong
blurb: Toasted mung beans and sticky rice softened into a coconut porridge.

steps.text: Rinse and drain the sticky rice. Sort the mung beans and check for stones.
Toast dry mung beans in a skillet over medium-low heat until fragrant and a shade darker. Crack them lightly with the base of a pot or a mortar.
Simmer the cracked beans in water, stirring occasionally, until they start to split and soften.
Add sticky rice and coconut milk. Simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is creamy and both grains and beans are fully soft. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick. Stir in sugar and salt.

title: Dinengdeng with Tilapia
blurb: An Ilocano bagoong broth with fresh greens and pan-seared tilapia.

steps.text: Trim the okra and string beans. Slice the eggplant and tomato. Pat the tilapia dry on a separate board.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan and cook the fish for around 4 minutes per side. Check it reaches 63°C and flakes easily. Transfer to a clean plate.
Bring water, tomato and bagoong to a boil in a pot. Add eggplant and beans, simmer 5 minutes, then add okra and cook until all vegetables are fork-tender. Slide in the tilapia for the final minute.

title: Pechay Miso Tofu Soup
blurb: A light soup with tender pechay, tofu, and mellow miso.

steps.text: Wash and chop the pechay, keeping stems and leaves separate. Cube the tofu and slice the scallion.
Bring water and the dried shiitake to a boil and simmer until the mushrooms soften. Lift them out with tongs, slice, and return to the pot.
Add tofu and pechay stems. Simmer until the stems are crisp-tender, then add the leaves for the final minute.
Whisk the miso into a small bowl of hot broth and stir it back into the pot off the heat. Top with scallion.

title: Mackerel Potato Patties
blurb: Crisp skillet patties made with canned mackerel and mashed potato.

steps.text: Peel and dice the potato. Drain the mackerel, flake it, and remove any firm bones. Slice scallion.
Cover the potato with water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, and simmer until a fork slides in easily. Drain and mash without milk.
Stir fish, potato, egg, scallion, pepper, and flour into a thick mixture and shape four small patties.
Warm a thin layer of oil over medium heat. Cook the patties on both sides until crisp and the center reaches 71°C. Keep them in one layer so they cook evenly.

title: Rice Cooker Garlic Chicken and Mushroom Rice
blurb: One-pot rice with garlic, mushrooms, and juicy chicken thigh.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and drain. Slice the mushrooms, garlic, and ginger. Cut the chicken into 2 cm pieces on a separate board, then wash hands and utensils.

Put rice, water and soy sauce into the rice cooker and scatter mushroom, aromatics, and chicken in a single layer. Close and run the regular white-rice cycle, following your cooker’s manual and fill marks. Check the largest chicken pieces reach 74°C. Continue heating until safe if needed.
Rest with the lid closed for 5 minutes. Fluff with a clean rice paddle and top with sliced scallion.
